requirements.notes: The verbatim Sec. 10-3 text (unlawful to contract without a current valid certificate of competency from the State CILB, the State Electrical Contractors Licensing Board, or the County CTQB; county certificate holders must also register with the State per FS 489.115/489.513; non-compliant bids on county/municipal public works are null and void) was read in a third-party copy; the CTQB Rules PDF (official) is the county's authoritative implementation of Chapter 10. requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County, RER — Board and Code Administration
requirements.applies_when: Any owner, authorized agent, or contractor constructing, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving, demolishing, or changing occupancy of a building in unincorporated Miami-Dade County (folios starting with '30')

forms.name: Building Permit Application (includes Notice of Commencement, Release of Lien, Affidavit, and guidelines)

requirements.notes: County process (per AO-04-115, official): file a complete application on the Building Department form with the required fee; application accompanied by two sets of complete plans and specifications; Building Department assigns a tracking processing number, reviews plans for code compliance, and routes them to Planning & Zoning and Environmental Resources Management (DERM) for new residential/commercial construction; applicant notified within 2 days of completion of the last review; if additional information is not submitted or the permit is not purchased within 60 calendar days of notification, the application/permit becomes null and void. In-person: Herbert S. Saffir Permitting and Inspection Center, 11805 SW 26 St, Miami 33175, 786-315-2000; Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st St, 11th Floor, 305-375-2877. Each municipality in the county has its own Building Official for work inside city limits.
requirements.timeline: Application becomes null and void 60 calendar days after readiness notification if not purchased/completed (AO-04-115)
requirements.title: Building permit application process (unincorporated county)

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County, RER — Construction, Permitting & Building Code Division
requirements.applies_when: A licensed/qualified contractor applying for subsidiary or stand-alone permits in the electrical, mechanical, plumbing, roofing, or gas trades (including subsidiary categories tied to a master building permit)
requirements.fees: Permit fees paid online by credit card or e-Check — amounts 'unverified'
requirements.notes: E-permitting lets qualified contractors apply online for subsidiary and stand-alone permits in the electrical, mechanical, plumbing, roofing and gas trades, pay fees, and print the permit card — no in-person visit. Available 7 days/week, 2 a.m. to 5 p.m. Forms are reviewed/approved programmatically if valid permit and jobsite data are entered. Stand-alone commercial reroofing cannot be obtained through e-permitting (subsidiary roofing tied to a master building permit only; Category 96 metal roof panels allowed for licensed roofing contractors). The general Portal supports 'Submit your permit or check status here' and 'Schedule/Cancel/Track Inspections'.
requirements.title: E-Permitting portal for qualified contractors

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County, RER — Construction, Permitting & Building Code Division; Miami-Dade Fire Rescue — Fire Prevention Division
requirements.applies_when: A construction business building new commercial structures, altering/adding to commercial buildings, or installing fire protection systems in unincorporated Miami-Dade County
requirements.citation: 'Miami-Dade County Permit - New Construction' (Fire Rescue); 'Find a Permit' index (miamidade.gov)
requirements.notes: Published commercial permit types: master Building Permit (new construction/addition/alteration) with trade categories (electrical, mechanical, plumbing, gas, roofing); Fire Rescue construction inspections for commercial buildings (final inspection required for Certificate of Occupancy; sprinkler system rough, underground, pressure test, and final; fire alarm inspection; standpipe; fire pump start-up; fire suppression system; temporary CO inspection; water main extension/fire hydrant; entrance features) — New Construction Bureau 786-315-2770. Fire final required for CO on all commercial buildings incl. apartments/townhomes; single-family homes not inspected by Fire Rescue. County also publishes optional plan-review accelerators: Concurrent Plans Processing (CPP, electronic multi-department routing), Concierge Plan Review for large commercial buildings, and Green Building Expedited review per County Code Sec. 8-6.

forms.name: Special Inspector Employment Notice (owner-hired special inspector)
Threshold (Special) Inspector Building Affidavit / Building Completion Statement

requirements.notes: Official sequence/logistics: an inspection is required before covering any part of construction; inspections performed 8 a.m.–3:30 p.m., Monday–Friday; approved plans and permit must be at the jobsite with the address posted and visible from the street; inspectors may conduct inspections wearing body cameras; inspectors take calls 7:00–8:00 a.m. only; routes are reordered 7:00–8:15 a.m. — verify the day's order after 8:15. For fire inspections: must be requested online the day prior before 4:00 p.m.; inspections scheduled the day before a county holiday roll to the next business day; an approved electrical rough inspection is required before scheduling a fire alarm inspection. Special/Threshold inspectors hired by the owner perform additional inspections under an approved structural inspection plan — these are in addition to mandatory county inspections; the threshold inspector submits an affidavit and completion statement; Certificate of Occupancy issued after all mandatory inspections pass. Live route tracking: 'Inspection Routes & Results' (permit/CO/boiler number shows today's route, inspector photo, and your stop).
requirements.timeline: Inspection requested day prior before 4:00 p.m. (fire); Building inspections M–F 8 a.m.–3:30 p.m.
requirements.title: Building inspection sequence, scheduling, and logistics

forms.name: Impact Fees Online Payment (requires process number)

requirements.notes: Impact fees must be paid in full before any building permit for development activity is issued. County collects for: Mobility (formerly road impact; countywide, all applications from Dec 31, 2023 assessed the mobility fee), Fire and Emergency Services (paid to the County for all municipalities except Miami, Miami Beach, Hialeah, Coral Gables, Key Biscayne which have their own fire departments), Police Services and Parks (usually paid to the cities directly — County currently collects for Palmetto Bay and Miami Lakes only), and Educational Facilities (transmitted to the School Board; paid countywide to the County). Each municipality may also impose its own impact fees — call the city with jurisdiction. Impact Fee Section: Miami-Dade Permitting and Inspection Center, 11805 SW 26 St, 786-315-2670, 7:30 a.m.–4 p.m. M–F.

requirements.agency: Miami-Dade County, RER — Contractor Licensing Section / Building Department
requirements.applies_when: A construction business or contractor applying for county building permits or renewing registrations
requirements.citation: Code of Miami-Dade County, Ch. 10 (contractor licensing); Florida AG Opinion re state-certified contractors and local requirements
requirements.notes: Interaction with round 1 local findings (do not duplicate): a construction business needs a Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax Receipt (BTR) for its place of business in addition to its trade credential — state-certified contractors exhibit the state license and pay the occupational (BTR) license fee plus building permit fee; county-credentialed (CTQB) contractors use their Certificate of Competency. Municipality building departments (e.g., Doral's published process, which mirrors county practice) require the license plus workers' compensation and liability insurance certificates to register and pull permits; workers' comp exemptions trigger a Notice to Owner filing with the permit application. County-specific: the CTQB 'misleading contractor names' rule (R10-107) bars business names that imply a scope of work the contractor is not certified for. Qualifying agent must have officer/partner/principal-stockholder interest in the entity (Ch. 10, Sec. 10-6(E)(5)).
requirements.title: Miami-Dade-specific contractor obligations (license + BTR + insurance at permit application)
